description: Named integer ceilings for Veles protocol v1. Values are JSON integers; the one value at the u64 extreme is a canonical unsigned decimal string (fixture/check convention) because JSON numbers cannot exactly represent it.

limits.name: pairing_window_seconds
limits.scope: per pairing window (phone)

limits.name: pairing_attempts_per_pairing_id
limits.scope: per pairing_id (phone)

limits.name: pairing_rolling_attempts_interval_seconds
limits.scope: phone rolling interval across pairing IDs

limits.name: pairing_rolling_attempts_max
limits.scope: phone within rolling five-minute interval across pairing IDs

limits.name: spake_operations_in_flight
limits.scope: phone, globally

limits.name: fresh_pa_per_connection
limits.scope: phone, per connection

limits.name: fresh_pa_rolling_interval_seconds
limits.scope: phone rolling interval across pairing IDs

limits.name: fresh_pa_rolling_max
limits.scope: phone within rolling one-minute interval across pairing IDs

limits.name: pairing_request_inactivity_timeout_seconds
limits.scope: per pairing handshake step

limits.name: pending_record_expiry_seconds
limits.scope: per pending or committed_waiting_ack trust record; a BOOT-SCOPED MONOTONIC deadline (creation + 86400 on the current boot's monotonic clock), with a persisted per-boot continuity token: incomplete records are deleted at boot/restart where continuity cannot be proven (OTP2-STA-010c). Client-side mapping (OTP2-STA-010d): the phone's authoritative below-active lifetime bounds the pair; genuinely-pending CLIENT records use a connector-owned monotonic interval (deleted on context loss); the client's durable active-family mirror has NO independent local deadline

limits.name: reconnect_idle_timeout_seconds
limits.scope: per protected session, no valid record either direction

limits.name: heartbeat_min_interval_seconds
limits.scope: per direction, per session

limits.name: push_ack_timeout_seconds
limits.scope: per outstanding push, per session

limits.name: push_max_retransmits
limits.scope: per queued event, per session

limits.name: otp_events_global
limits.scope: all endpoints, global buffer

limits.name: otp_max_lifetime_seconds
limits.scope: per event, all endpoints

limits.name: record_max_bytes
limits.scope: total protected record size (header+ciphertext+tag); also reassembled record total, and the GATT send ceiling of decoded `send` records: after envelope admission (bridge_record_max_bytes), the bridge's GATT send path refuses 4097..5120 with correlated oversize_record before any fragment is created or written — the envelope parser never refuses that range

limits.name: record_ciphertext_max_bytes
limits.scope: per protected record ciphertext (record_max_bytes minus 23-byte header and 16-byte tag)

limits.name: sequence_max
limits.scope: per direction, per session (u64; string because JSON numbers cannot represent it exactly)
limits.note: Counters never wrap; the direction that issued sequence_max terminates before any further record.

limits.name: gatt_max_clients
limits.scope: phone GATT service, simultaneous clients

limits.name: gatt_mtu_min
limits.scope: negotiated ATT MTU, per connection

limits.name: gatt_mtu_max
limits.scope: largest negotiated ATT MTU an implementation accepts (Android requestMtu ceiling); a larger reported value is refused like one below the floor

limits.name: fragment_payload_bytes_at_min_mtu
limits.scope: non-final fragment payload at the MTU floor 185 (185 - 3 ATT header - 4 fragment header); the tested conservative chunk (M1): the largest record needs <= ceil(4096/178) = 24 fragments

limits.name: gatt_attribute_value_max_bytes
limits.scope: one fragment frame (4-byte header + payload) in either direction: min(negotiated ATT MTU - 3, 512), the Bluetooth ATT maximum attribute value length (profile revision 2, OTP-23)

limits.name: fragment_payload_bytes_at_attribute_max
limits.scope: non-final fragment payload whenever the attribute budget is clamped, i.e. every negotiated ATT MTU >= 515 (512 attribute bytes - 4 fragment header)

limits.name: fragment_index_max
limits.scope: per transaction

limits.name: fragment_transaction_count_max_per_peer
limits.scope: incomplete fragment transactions per peer (TOTAL across the peer's inbound traffic, not per direction) (OTP2-GAT-012)

limits.name: reassembly_incomplete_max_per_peer
limits.scope: incomplete reassemblies per peer (TOTAL across the peer's inbound traffic, not per direction) (OTP2-GAT-012)

limits.name: reassembly_bytes_max_per_peer
limits.scope: reassembly buffer bytes per peer (TOTAL across the peer's inbound traffic, not per direction) (OTP2-GAT-012)

limits.name: reassembly_incomplete_max_global
limits.scope: incomplete reassemblies, phone global

limits.name: reassembly_bytes_max_global
limits.scope: reassembly buffer bytes, phone global

limits.name: deliver_queue_messages_max_per_peer
limits.scope: transport delivery queue per peer

limits.name: deliver_queue_bytes_max_per_peer
limits.scope: transport delivery queue per peer

limits.name: deliver_queue_messages_max_global
limits.scope: transport delivery queue, phone global

limits.name: deliver_queue_bytes_max_global
limits.scope: transport delivery queue, phone global

limits.name: fragment_timeout_seconds
limits.scope: between consecutive fragments of one transaction (monotonic, millisecond precision)

limits.name: disconnect_cleanup_max_seconds
limits.scope: per peer state erasure after link loss

limits.name: frame_total_max_bytes
limits.scope: pre-auth plaintext frame total (tag+length+payload)

limits.name: spake_context_max_bytes
limits.scope: canonical public context (AAD); inside RFC 9382's 8168-byte AAD bound

limits.name: identity_label_max_bytes
limits.scope: UTF-8 label in enroll_identity

limits.name: otp_code_max_bytes
limits.scope: UTF-8 OTP code in an OTP event

limits.name: otp_merchant_max_bytes
limits.scope: UTF-8 merchant in an OTP event

limits.name: otp_amount_scale_max
limits.scope: per OTP event

limits.name: bridge_message_max_bytes
limits.scope: one Native Messaging JSON message, both directions (stricter than Chrome's 1 MiB host-to-extension limit)

limits.name: bridge_record_max_bytes
limits.scope: record_base64 decoded bytes, per bridge send/message; the envelope admission ceiling only — a send decoding above record_max_bytes (4096) is refused by the bridge's GATT send layer with correlated oversize_record before any fragment is created or written

limits.name: bridge_outstanding_requests_max
limits.scope: bridge process, concurrent outstanding

limits.name: bridge_open_scans_max
limits.scope: bridge process

limits.name: bridge_open_connections_max
limits.scope: bridge process

limits.name: bridge_request_timeout_seconds
limits.scope: per bridge request (scans exempt)

limits.name: bridge_scan_max_seconds
limits.scope: per scan

limits.name: bridge_device_found_rate_max
limits.scope: per scan, rolling second

limits.name: bridge_device_found_per_scan_max
limits.scope: per scan

limits.name: bridge_discovered_devices_max
limits.scope: per process, currently discovered device handles retained in the bounded discovery cache (FIFO eviction of the oldest entry not currently connected; independent of the per-scan event cap)

limits.name: bridge_output_queue_messages_max
limits.scope: bridge pending outbound JSON

limits.name: bridge_output_queue_bytes_max
limits.scope: bridge pending outbound bytes

limits.name: bridge_platform_hint_max_bytes
limits.scope: platform_hint strings (byte length, OTP2-BRD-002a; not code points or UTF-16 units)

limits.name: bridge_advertisement_max_bytes
limits.scope: decoded advertisement metadata per device_found

limits.name: bridge_error_stage_max_bytes
limits.scope: error stage string (ASCII alphabet, byte length = character count here)

limits.name: app_error_reason_max_bytes
limits.scope: UTF-8 reason in app_error record

limits.name: pull_outstanding_max
limits.scope: per session, unanswered pull

limits.name: push_outstanding_max
limits.scope: per session, un-acked push

limits.name: fragment_transaction_id_min
limits.scope: valid transaction_id values start at 1 (0 rejects)

limits.name: pending_record_max_bytes
limits.scope: maximum enroll_identity body size (label_len included)

limits.name: pending_record_body_max_bytes
limits.scope: maximum enroll_identity body size (label included; minimum 132)

limits.name: bridge_input_frame_queue_max
limits.scope: bridge process, reader-side staged Native Messaging input frames (the deterministic core's backpressure queue before the strict parser)

limits.name: bridge_input_frame_queue_bytes_max
limits.scope: reader-side staged input frames' total bytes, per process

limits.name: bridge_data_events_max
limits.scope: bridge process, staged backend fragment data events (OS callback ingress, each at most the 512-byte fragment-frame ceiling; committed plus in-transit deferred fragments; exactly 32 links x the per-link ceiling, so every link can sit at its own cap at once). Ingress staging only - unrelated to the frozen reassembly (2 / 8 KiB per peer, 16 / 64 KiB global) and delivery caps

limits.name: bridge_data_events_bytes_max
limits.scope: staged backend fragment data events' total bytes, per process (32 links x 16 KiB); independent of the 1536-event ceiling

limits.name: bridge_data_events_per_link_max
limits.scope: staged backend fragment data events, per connection stream (its bounded ingress FIFO); 48 = two maximum 4096-byte records at the 185-byte MTU floor (2 x 24 fragments)

limits.name: bridge_data_events_bytes_per_link_max
limits.scope: staged backend fragment data events' bytes, per connection stream; independent of the event ceiling (48 x 512 = 24576 > 16384, so 512-byte fragments reach this cap at 32 events)

limits.name: bridge_gate_staged_data_events_max
limits.scope: per link/scan callback admission gate: fragment/advertisement events staged before the opening event and queued in the gate's in-transit lane; equal to the per-link ingress ceiling so a burst the ingress accepts is never refused earlier

limits.name: bridge_gate_staged_data_bytes_max
limits.scope: per link/scan callback admission gate: staged fragment bytes (same bound as the per-link ingress byte ceiling)

limits.name: bridge_deferred_controls_max
limits.scope: process-wide control/terminal slots of the ingress in-transit lane (events emitted while the ingress state lock is busy); data can never occupy them; exhausting them latches the control-overflow host failure

limits.name: bridge_controls_per_scan_max
limits.scope: reserved control FIFO slots, per scan (start/failed/ended lifecycle)

limits.name: bridge_controls_per_link_max
limits.scope: reserved control FIFO slots, per connection stream (connected/connect_failed/capacity_changed/link_lost/link_released); a control beyond the cap latches the process-level control-overflow exit (host failure)

limits.name: bridge_send_completions_per_link_max
limits.scope: guaranteed per-link send-completion staging (WriteDone/WriteFailed), one per admitted outstanding request so a completion is never displaced by ordinary traffic

limits.name: bridge_send_storage_records_per_link
limits.scope: bridge send storage (pending + in-flight records), per connection

limits.name: bridge_send_storage_bytes_per_link
limits.scope: bridge send storage bytes, per connection

limits.name: bridge_send_storage_records_global
limits.scope: bridge send storage records, process-wide

limits.name: bridge_send_storage_bytes_global
limits.scope: bridge send storage bytes, process-wide

limits.name: bridge_discovery_staging_max
limits.scope: bounded latest-wins advertisement staging set per scan (distinct devices; duplicates coalesce in place)
